title: Sprint Ops GPU Handshake Playtest — 2026-12-08
content:
Objective:
Summary notes from the sprint ops playtest focused on cross-region GPU handshake behavior, capacity choreography, and emergency preemption rehearsals. Goal was to validate automated routing policy + canary fallback in a simulated surge and verify operator runbook clarity. This is a working log — rough, contains hypotheses and open questions.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner, ops lead)
- Diego Morales (fleet infra)
- Emma Chen (capacity planning)
- Ravi Srinivasan (SRE)
- Laila Arif (runtime) — joined for kernel failover checks
- Observers: Solutions-eng rotation

Agenda:
1) Short overview of handshake flow and new routing flags (5m)
2) Run surge simulation v3 across three regions (30m)
3) Validate canary fallback and degraded-variance routing (20m)
4) Triage issues, assign owners and followups (15m)

Key results (high level):
- Handshake timing: average inter-region handshake (route diff + model variant negotiation) = 210ms under baseline, spikes to ~680ms during synthetic serialization storm. This exceeds our SLO for cold-start sensitive routes.
- Canary fallback: succeeded in 88% of canary trials. Failures (12%) were due to stale quantized model artifact staged in eu-west-1 that missed the rollout tag — root cause: artifact registry tag collision during concurrent deploy.
- Preemption rehearsal: preemptible spot reclaim simulation triggered graceful fallback in west-us and re-routed 32% of live requests to dedicated pool; token latency increased by median +110ms but p99 stayed under target for majority routes.
- Autoscaler oscillation observed when transient surge < 90s; autoscaler launched small pods then tore them down repeatedly. Need hysteresis tuning.

Capacity snapshot used for simulation:
- west-us (primary): 320 x A100-equivalent, burst reserve 48 GPUs (dedicated pool)
- eu-west-1: 210 x A100-equivalent, canary pool 12 GPUs (quantized variants)
- apac-northeast: 64 x H100-equivalent (edge-limited), edge pool 24 x T4 for low-cost inference
- spare (regional buffer): 36 GPUs across zones (unallocated)

What we tested:
- Route policy: latency-first with cost-floor fallback to quantized model variant
- Fallback policy: gradual-stepdown (20% -> 50% -> 100%) over 120s window
- KV cache priming: disabled for first two iterations, enabled on iteration 3
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic to canary variant with shadowed metrics
- Preemption: simulated node reclaim at random times between 30–180s after run start

Observed anomalies (details):
1) Artifact registry collision (eu-west-1):
   - Symptom: canary instances started with legacy quantized-v1 instead of quantized-v2
   - Impact: incorrect output formatting for function-call tests, caused automatic regression alert to fire
   - Immediate mitigation: pinned canary to explicit digest (sha256:...) and rolled forward; longer-term: registry tagging policy review + atomic deploy gating (owner: Diego, due 2026-12-17)

2) Autoscaler thrash (west-us):
   - Symptom: pod churn when surge ~60–80s; scale-up followed by quick scale-down
   - Hypothesis: scale-down timeout < typical request backlog decay for batched queues
   - Action: increase scale-down stabilization window from 45s -> 180s for batching-heavy pools (owner: Ravi, due 2026-12-14)

3) Handshake jitter when KV priming toggled:
   - Symptom: handshake 210ms -> 680ms when priming enabled under load
   - Notes: likely due to blocking IO on cache warm path; Laila to profile runtime lock contention and async prewarm paths (owner: Laila, due 2026-12-13)

Operational play additions (runbook edits):
- Add explicit step for verifying registry digest during canary start (include example gcloud/az cli commands).
- Append hystereses guidance for autoscaler tuning keyed by median request length and batch size.
- Add a triage checklist for handshake jitter: check KV cache metrics, network egress queue, kernel selection logs.

Action items (triage + next steps):
- Diego: Implement atomic-tag gating for registry and add a quick health-check for canary artifact digest. Target: 2026-12-17.
- Ravi: Update autoscaler stabilization window + run two short regression sims. Target: 2026-12-14.
- Laila: Profile runtime KV prewarm path and propose async warm-up patch or lock-fine-grain fix. Target: 2026-12-13.
- Emma: Re-run capacity projection with surge profiles A/B (30m vs 120m surges) and publish recommended buffer changes for APAC edge. Target: 2026-12-16.
- Aisha: Draft updated runbook excerpt and circulate for review. Target: 2026-12-12.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the acceptable handshake latency budget for cold-start-sensitive routes? Current SLOs say "sub-300ms" for 95th percentile; do we relax for backing fallback (quantized) routes? (Decision owner: Product + Eng infra)
- Should canary traffic percentage increase to 20% to stress artifact resolution earlier? Pros: surface artifact issues faster. Cons: larger blast radius. (Discuss in next ops sync)

Simulation notes / artifacts:
- Simulation logs uploaded: gs://redwood-sim-results/2026-12-08/handshake-playtest-v3.tar.gz
- Runbook diff (wip): GitHub PR redwood/runbooks#282 — includes sample commands and triage checklist
- Dashboard panels created: infra.handshake.latency, infra.autoscaler.churn, infra.canary.artifact-mismatch

Casual/notes-to-self:
- Observed that small H100 pools in APAC saturate quickly for long-context workloads; maybe prioritize quantized variants for these routes.
- Need to coordinate with Solutions-eng before changing canary %, they're shipping a demo next week that pins a model tag.

Meeting recording: internal drive link (private) — shared in #fleet-ops slack thread after review.
